claims.text: The target starting composition is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding nominally to 20 at.% of each element.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi contains minimal intrinsic short-range order.
The as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has relatively low hardness and yield strength.
The relatively low hardness and yield strength of as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are caused primarily by the absence of significant short-range order.
Chemical short-range order creates atomic-scale obstacles that pin dislocations and impede their glide.
Annealing CoCrFeNiTi at 600 °C for 24 hours will induce appreciable short-range order.
The proposed 600 °C annealing treatment can produce short-range order without nucleating secondary precipitates.
Increasing short-range order in the matrix will increase dislocation pinning.
The increased dislocation pinning produced by short-range order will raise hardness and compressive yield strength.
Short-range-order strengthening will reduce plastic strain relative to the as-cast alloy.
Annealing is expected to increase hardness and compressive yield strength by approximately 10–20% over the as-cast state.
Short-range order can be verified and quantified using high-resolution TEM and X-ray or neutron diffuse scattering.
A prior mechanical-testing protocol used room- and elevated-temperature compression at a quasi-static strain rate of 2 × 10^-4 s^-1 with three replicate tests.
The controlled comparison is limited to quasi-static compression at 25 °C and 600 °C on untreated and annealed specimens of the same nominal composition.
The baseline alloy has high ductility and machinability despite relatively low hardness and strength.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on the kinetics of short-range-order formation.
Annealing may instead produce unwanted secondary precipitation.

Failure of verified increases in short-range order to correlate with statistically significant increases in hardness and yield strength would falsify short-range-order absence as the main cause of low strength.
